summary: Grant County, OR: 1930s pole tower with L-4 cab; fell in the mid-1960s, a later 1980 tower removed about 2005; no source describes the site today.

facts.design: 30-ft pole tower with L-4 cab (register and firelookout.com); the register adds a 14x14 ft cab; a 1935 newspaper item says 40 ft
facts.status_note: Tower fell down in the mid-1960s; a later 1980 tower was removed about 2005. No source describes the site today.

corrections.why: The register and firelookout.com both describe a 30-foot pole tower, about 9.1 m. No source we read gives 4.3 m. A 1935 newspaper item quoted by weebly says 40 feet (about 12.2 m), which the story reports as a disagreement.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and firelookout.com say a 30-foot pole tower; a 1935 newspaper item quoted by weebly says a 40-foot tower. Facts use 30 ft; the story gives both.
The register and firelookout.com say Umatilla National Forest; the weebly page says Whitman National Forest. The story gives both and does not choose.

notes_for_editor: No source we read covers staffing, so the story leaves it out. No source describes what remains at the site or whether it is public; access is omitted. Do not confuse this with a different Silver Butte near Riddle in Douglas County (weebly page silver-butte1.html). A 2013 cherylhill.net post about an Oregon Department of Forestry tear-down of a Silver Butte lookout is probably that other site; it was not used. The brief's height_m of 4.3 has no source.
